rules.statement: When a change adds behavior on a failure or conflict path, add a test whose fixture actually reaches that path and checks the new behavior, so that removing the new code makes the test fail.
rules.why: An untested branch can regress silently. Here, losing the staging call on conflict would leave new files untracked and out of the update commit.
rules.check: For each new statement in an error, conflict or fallback branch, look for a test fixture that drives execution into that branch and asserts its effect. A fixture that enters the branch but never triggers the new behavior (for example, one that adds no files) doesn't count.

rules.statement: When help text, comments, README or CHANGELOG state a guarantee that code never does something, make sure no code path in the change still does it, or narrow the documented wording to match.
rules.why: A false documented guarantee misleads users, and anyone auditing for that behavior has to check every path again.
rules.check: Search the changed scripts or code for the construct the docs say is never used (for example `git add -A`), including in rarely run branches such as conflict handling.

rules.statement: Don't ask for a CHANGELOG entry to move under `## [Unreleased]` when the repository cuts a release per plan or per PR: there, previous entries are written in dated version sections and `[Unreleased]` stays empty.
rules.why: Such repositories release every plan, so a dated section for the release the plan names is correct, not a release that doesn't exist.
rules.check: Before reporting, check whether earlier CHANGELOG sections were added the same way with `[Unreleased]` left empty, and whether the plan or PR names that version on a `Release:` line.
